messages:
jia: Quick heads-up — I ran a perf profile on master after the kernel-selector tweak. Streaming endpoints (stream-v2) p95 regressed from ~210ms -> ~260ms on p3.2xlarge for seq=512. Looks correlated with batch formation behavior (token targets bumped to 160).
omar: Can you drop the traces or a short flame?
jia: Paste of the lightweight trace:
```
queue_wait_ms: 42
kv_lock_ms: 6
kernel_select_ms: 12
partial_decode_ms: 8
```
(small sample, but consistent across runs)
sophia: Huh. My hunch: continuous-batcher waiting for token_budget_per_batch >= 160 is increasing the latency tail for streamed responses because partial-decode preemption rarely triggers early flush. Streaming wants smaller batch targets + more aggressive partial-decode scheduling.
jia: Also seeing more KV cache contention on streams: prefetch/update race when stream gets preempted. That adds ~5-10ms occasionally.
omar: I'll repro with synthetic load: 60rps, 30% streaming, interleaved short/long prompts. If we reproduce, we can test lowering token target.
eng-bot: load test queued: id=lt-8793 - results pending

sophia: Quick staging experiment: set batch_token_target=120, partial_decode_weight=1.2, stream_priority=HIGH. Result: p95 down to ~225ms, throughput steady. No spike in GPU utilization.
jia: Nice. So two levers helped: reduce token target and boost partial-decode priority. Also need KV prefetch backoff on preempted streams.
omar: I'll open a tiny config PR + a canary rollout that toggles batch_token_target per-route for streaming routes.
sophia: Also add a kernel-selection override for streamed responses — current avg_seq heuristic sometimes picks the large-kernel optimized for long sequences even when the batch is small, adding kernel_switch overhead. Prefer small-kernel for stream routes.
eng-bot: PR opened: #1234 by omar

jia: Ops plan: canary the config change on 5% of host pool for 30m, monitor p95 and tail error rate, fallback if p95 > 300ms. If canary good, roll to 25% then 100%.
omar: I'll include an integration test that simulates streaming + KV prefetch races and asserts no tail regression. link to draft: https://git.company/repo/pull/1234
sophia: Also adding a short doc snippet in runtime tuning about interactions: "streaming + continuous batching = prefer lower batch token targets, partial-decode promotion, kernel override, KV prefetch backoff". Saves future confusion.
jia: Agreed. One more observation: kernel selector metrics show a small bump in kernel_select_ms after the change; I'm adding more logging to correlate selection decisions to batch shape.
omar: I'll run the staging perf job tomorrow morning and post results. Thanks all :thumbsup:
